verses.zh: 那日，必给大卫家和耶路撒冷的居民开一个泉源，洗除罪恶与污秽。
verses.en: “In that day there will be a fountain opened up for the dynasty[NOTE:1] of David and the people of Jerusalem[NOTE:2] to cleanse them from sin and impurity.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “house” (so NIV, NRSV), referring to dynastic descendants.
For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

Heb “for sin and for impurity.” The purpose implied here has been stated explicitly in the translation for clarity.sn This reference to the fountain opened up…to cleanse them from sin and impurity is anticipatory of the cleansing from sin that lies at the heart of the NT gospel message (Rom 10:9-10; Titus 3:5). “In that day” throughout the passage (vv. 1, 2, 4) locates this cleansing in the eschatological (church) age (John 19:37).

verses.zh: 万军之耶和华说：「那日，我必从地上除灭偶像的名，不再被人记念；也必使这地不再有假先知与污秽的灵。
verses.en: And also on that day,” says the Lord of Heaven’s Armies, “I will remove[NOTE:1] the names of the idols from the land and they will never again be remembered. Moreover, I will remove the prophets and the unclean spirit from the land.

verses.zh: 若再有人说预言，生他的父母必对他说：『你不得存活，因为你托耶和华的名说假预言。』生他的父母在他说预言的时候，要将他刺透。
verses.en: Then, if anyone prophesies in spite of this, his father and mother to whom he was born will say to him, ‘You cannot live, for you lie in the name of the Lord.’ Then his father and mother to whom he was born will run him through with a sword when he prophesies.[NOTE:1]
notes: Death (in this case being run…through with a sword) was the penalty required in the OT for prophesying falsely (Deut 13:6-11; 18:20-22).

verses.zh: 那日，凡作先知说预言的必因他所论的异象羞愧，不再穿毛衣哄骗人。
verses.en: “Therefore, on that day each prophet will be ashamed of his vision when he prophesies and will no longer wear the hairy garment[NOTE:1] of a prophet to deceive the people.[NOTE:2]
notes: The “hairy garment of a prophet” (אַדֶּרֶת שֵׁעָר, ʾadderet sheʿar) was the rough clothing of Elijah (1 Kgs 19:13), Elisha (1 Kgs 19:19; 2 Kgs 2:14), and even John the Baptist (Matt 3:4). Yet אַדֶּרֶת alone suggests something of beauty and honor (Josh 7:21). The prophet’s attire may have been simple; the image it conveyed was one of great dignity.
The words “the people” are not in the Hebrew text, but are supplied in the translation from context (cf. NCV, TEV, NLT).

verses.zh: 他必说：『我不是先知，我是耕地的；我从幼年作人的奴仆。』
verses.en: Instead he will say, ‘I am no prophet; indeed, I am a farmer, for a man has made me his indentured servant since my youth.’[NOTE:1]
notes: Or perhaps “for the land has been my possession since my youth” (so NRSV; similar NAB).

verses.zh: 必有人问他说：『你两臂中间是甚么伤呢？』他必回答说：『这是我在亲友家中所受的伤。』」
verses.en: Then someone will ask him, ‘What are these wounds on your chest?’[NOTE:1] and he will answer, ‘Some that I received in the house of my friends.’
notes: These wounds on your chest. Pagan prophets were often self-lacerated (Lev 19:28; Deut 14:1; 1 Kgs 18:28) for reasons not entirely clear, so this false prophet betrays himself as such by these graphic and ineradicable marks.tn Heb “wounds between your hands.” Cf. NIV “wounds on your body”; KJV makes this more specific: “wounds in thine hands.”

verses.zh: 万军之耶和华说：刀剑哪，应当兴起，攻击我的牧人和我的同伴。击打牧人，羊就分散；我必反手加在微小者的身上。
verses.en: “Awake, sword, against my shepherd,against the man who is my associate,”says the Lord of Heaven’s Armies.“Strike the shepherd that the flock may be scattered;[NOTE:1] I will turn my hand against the insignificant ones.
notes: Despite the NT use of this text to speak of the scattering of the disciples following Jesus’ crucifixion (Matt 26:31; Mark 14:27), the immediate context of Zechariah suggests that unfaithful shepherds (kings) will be punished by the Lord precisely so their flocks (disobedient Israel) can be scattered (cf. Zech 11:6, 8, 9, 16). It is likely that Jesus drew on this passage merely to make the point that whenever shepherds are incapacitated, sheep will scatter. Thus he was not identifying himself with the shepherd in this text (the shepherd in the Zechariah text is a character who is portrayed negatively).

verses.zh: 耶和华说：这全地的人，三分之二必剪除而死，三分之一仍必存留。
verses.en: It will happen in all the land,” says the Lord,“that two-thirds of the people[NOTE:1] in it will be cut off and die,but one-third will be left in it.[NOTE:2]
notes: The words “of the people” are supplied in the translation for clarity (cf. NCV, TEV, NLT).

The fractions mentioned here call to mind the affliction of God’s people described by Ezekiel, though Ezekiel referred to his own times whereas Zechariah is looking forward to a future eschatological age. Ezekiel spoke of cutting his hair at God’s command (Ezek 5:1-4) and then of burning a third of it, striking a third with a sword, and scattering the rest. From this last third a few hairs would survive to become the nucleus of a new Israel. It is this “third” Zechariah speaks of (v. 9), the remnant who will be purified and reclaimed as God’s covenant people.

verses.zh: 我要使这三分之一经火，熬炼他们，如熬炼银子；试炼他们，如试炼金子。他们必求告我的名，我必应允他们。我要说：这是我的子民。他们也要说：耶和华是我们的　神。
verses.en: Then I will bring the remaining third into the fire;I will refine them like silver is refinedand will test them like gold is tested.They will call on my name and I will answer;I will say, ‘These are my people,’and they will say, ‘The Lord is our God.’”[NOTE:1]
notes: The expression I will say ‘It is my people,’ and they will say ‘the Lord is our God’ is reminiscent of the restoration of Israel predicted by Hosea, who said that those who had been rejected as God’s people would be reclaimed and once more become his sons and daughters (Hos 2:23).

READING CYCLE THREE (see
"Bible
Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which
means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the
light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not
relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare
your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is
the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every
paragraph has one and only one subject.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: ZECHARIAH 13:1

1"In that day a fountain will be opened for the house of David and
for the inhabitants of Jerusalem, for sin and for impurity.

13:1 "In that day" This is the repeated eschatological marker of chapters 10-14 (cf. Zech. 13:2).

▣ "a fountain will be opened" The concept of a fountain of life (i.e., living waters, cf. John 4:10,14) comes
from Isa. 12:2-3; Jer. 2:13 (for the negative see Jer. 51:36; Hosea 13:15); and Jer. 17:13. YHWH is the source of life
(cf. Genesis 1-2 and Ps. 36:5-9).

In this context the fountain refers to the forgiveness of sin (i.e., by washing or drinking), which is obviously
related to the repentance mentioned in Zech. 12:10. This is imagery for the New Covenant of Jer. 31:31-34; Ezek. 36:22-36
(cf. Rom. 11:26-27; Eph. 5:26; Titus 3:5).

The VERB (BDB 834 I, KB 986, Niphal PARTICPLE) also
connected to it is a Qal IMPERFECT, "to be" (BDB 224, KB 243), which denotes an
emphasis of permanently opened! God's life-giving water will now flow forever (cf. Zech. 14:8; Ezek. 47:1-12;
Rev. 22:1; Ps. 46:4).

▣ "for the house of David and for the inhabitants of Jerusalem" The royal line and the people
who returned from exile are the recipients (cf. Zech. 12:10). Notice there is no distinction between
Jerusalem and Judah, as in Zech. 12:2,5,7.

▣ "for sin" This is the common Hebrew term (BDB 308) which means "to miss the goal," "to miss
the mark," or "to miss the way" (cf. BDB 306).

▣ "for impurity" This Hebrew term (BDB 622) was used mostly of ceremonial defilement by
menstrual flow (NIDOTTE, vol. 1, pp. 925-928), but was also used for idolatry (cf. 2 Chr. 29:5-6; Ezra 9:11).

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: ZECHARIAH 13:2-6

2"It will come about in that day," declares the
Lord of hosts, "that I will cut off the names of the idols from the land, and they will no longer be remembered;
and I will also remove the prophets and the unclean spirit from the land. 3And if anyone still prophesies, then his father and
mother who gave birth to him will say to him, ‘You shall not live, for you have spoken falsely in the name of the Lord';
and his father and mother who gave birth to him will pierce him through when he prophesies. 4Also it will come about in that
day that the prophets will each be ashamed of his vision when he prophesies, and they will not put on a hairy robe in order to deceive;
5but he will say, ‘I am not a prophet; I am a tiller of the ground, for a man sold me as a slave in my youth.' 6And
one will say to him, ‘What are these wounds between your arms?' Then he will say, ‘Those with which I was wounded in the house of my friends.'"

13:2 "it will come about in that day, declares the Lord of hosts" This is
the continuing use of the eschatological phrase, "that day," combined with the common post-exilic title for Israel's
God, which implies military power.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THAT DAY

SPECIAL TOPIC: LORD OF HOSTS

▣ "that I will cut off the names of the idols from the land" The VERB "cut off"
(BDB 503, KB 500, Hiphil IMPERFECT) means to remove and destroy the idols and their
followers (cf. Micah 5:10-15; Zeph. 1:4-6).

Again, the time setting of Zechariah 9-14 is very difficult to ascertain. It is obvious that
idol worship was a major problem with the Jewish people before the Exile, but after the Exile this was not
a problem. This verse seems to imply that idolatry will again become a major sin of the people of God.

This context is similar to Ezek. 36:22-36 in that YHWH chooses to act Himself because of His
people's inadequacy to act. In Ezekiel He acts on their behalf to inaugurate the New Covenant
(cf. Jer. 31:31-34). Here He acts to remove evil from their midst (i.e., idols, false prophets, and the
unclean spirit).

▣ "and I will also remove the prophets" The VERB (BDB 716, Hiphil #4,
IMPERFECT, KB 778) is used of removing evil people in 1 Kgs. 15:12 and 2 Chr. 15:8.

This obviously refers to false prophets (cf. LXX). The discussion in Zech. 13:3-6 deals with
those who claim to know and speak for YHWH, but who are actually a tool for the evil one (cf. Matt. 24:4-5,11,23-24).

▣ "and the unclean spirit from the land" The presence of the DEFINITE ARTICLE
could mean that we are identifying a particular figure (i.e., Satan, cf. 1 Kgs. 22:21) or this is a hendiadys,
which means "the prophets" and "the unclean spirit" form one group (i.e., false prophets). This same phrase
is also used quite often in the NT to refer to the demonic. It (i.e., Leupold, p. 246, "spirit of
uncleanness") is obvious that this is the exact opposite of "the spirit of grace" mentioned in Zech. 12:10.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SATAN

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE DEMONIC IN THE OT

13:3 "And it will come about that if anyone still prophesies, then his father and mother" A tremendous
change of attitude has occurred where even parents are ready to discipline their children for idol worship.

There are several similarities between this paragraph and Zech. 12:10-14. It almost seems
that a true prophet suffered the fate of the false prophets.

▣ "You shall not live, for you have spoken falsely in the name of the Lord"
This refers to the punishment for false prophets from Deut. 13:1-10; 18:20,22. The only difference is that in
Zech. 13:3 the offender is pierced, while in Deuteronomy they are stoned.

SPECIAL TOPIC: "THE NAME" OF YHWH (OT)

▣ "pierce him through" This is the same VERB (BDB 201, KB 230, Qal
PERFECT; NIDOTTE, vol. 1, p. 983) used in Zech. 12:10 and the implication is that he is pierced by his
parents because he is a false prophet and a blasphemer. This may be so that the whole family may not be judged
(cf. Jer. 23:34). This is exactly the reason that the Jews crucified Jesus because they saw Him as a false
prophet and a blasphemer.

This is a different VERB than Isa. 53:5 (see exegetical note online).

13:4 "in that day that the prophets will each be ashamed of his vision when he prophesies"
Zechariah 13:4-6 describe the excuses that these false prophets will make when they are confronted with
their false prophecies. A good descriptive parallel to "ashamed" (BDB 101) prophets is Micah 3:5-7.

▣ "a hairy robe" This was (BDB 12 CONSTRUCT BDB 972) the distinctive dress of
some prophets.

- Samuel, 1 Sam. 28:14 (different word)

- Elijah, 1 Kgs. 19:13; 2 Kgs. 1:8; 2:8

- Elisha, 1 Kgs. 19:19; 2 Kgs. 2:13,14

- John the Baptist, Matt. 3:4; Mark 1:6

13:5 "I am not a prophet; I am a tiller of the ground" This man will claim to be a farmer, not a
prophet.

The JPSOA footnote suggests that this phrase was a way of linking the speaker to Noah
(cf. Gen. 9:20-21, where the same phrase is used). If this is true, then JPSOA adds

"i.e. I was addicted to wine like Noah, the tiller of the soil, hense my
hallucinations and cravings, cf. Prov. 23:33."

▣

NASB
"for a man sold me as a slave in my youth"

NKJV
"man taught me to keep cattle from my youth"

NRSV
"for the land has been my possession since my youth"

TEV
"I have farmed the land all my life"

NJB
"for the land has been my living since I was a boy"

REB
"for the land has been my possession from my early days"

JPSOA
"I was plied with the red stuff from my youth on"

LXX
"because such a person brought me up from my youth"

Peshitta
"and a man made me zealous to prophesy from my youth"

This phrase is very ambiguous, but it is related to the phrase, "a tiller of the ground."
The differences are because of the possible origins of "buy as a slave" (hqnni, BDB 888, KB 1111,
Hiphil PERFECT).

- NKJV, connects it to mqnh (BDB 889), a flock or herd

- NASB, connects it to qnh (BDB 888, KB 1114), acquire or purchase

- NRSV, slightly changes the MT by adding one consonant

F. F. Bruce, Answers to Questions, makes a good point,

"The clause is an amplification of the preceding one ('I am a tiller of the ground')
and means that the speaker is a simple agricultural laborer and no prophet" (p. 38).

The UBS Text Project, p. 422, gives the MT (NASB) a "B" rating (some doubt).

13:6 "And one will say to him, 'What are these wounds between your arms'" The false prophet will
be easily recognized by special cultic marks on his body. "Between his hands" is a Hebrew idiom (BDB 388)
for somewhere on his back, chest, arms, or hands. There seem to be two OT allusions to this practice:

- the prophets of Ba'al (cf. 1 Kgs. 18:28; NIDOTTE, vol. 1, pp. 819-820)

- special pagan practices for mourning (cf. Lev. 19:28; 21:5; Deut. 14:1; Jer. 16:6; 41:5; 48:37)

The JPSOA footnote sees these "sores" (BDB 646) as related to 2 Kgs. 9:24. It adds "sores
are sometimes symptoms of hysteria."

▣ "Then he will say, 'Those with which I was wounded in the house of my friends'" He tries
to explain his wounds by saying he received them while meeting with his friends (Hebrew is
MASCULINE). However, the term "friends" or "lovers" (BDB 12, Piel) is used in the OT
for associates in idolatry (cf. Jer. 22:20,22; 30:14; Ezek. 16:33,36,37; 23:5,9,22; Hosea 2:7,9,12,14,15;
also LXX of Hosea 7:14).

The JPSOA footnote sees this as the result of the man causing a drunken scene (i.e., Prov. 23:35).

The ambiguity of this figurative language can be seen in that some commentators refer it to
false prophets (NET), but others to the wounded Messiah betrayed by His own.

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: ZECHARIAH 13:7-9

7"Awake, O sword, against My Shepherd,

And against the man, My Associate,"

Declares the Lord of hosts.

"Strike the Shepherd that the sheep may be scattered;

And I will turn My hand against the little ones.

8It will come about in all the land,"

Declares the Lord, "

That two parts in it will be cut off and perish;

But the third will be left in it.

9And I will bring the third part through the fire,

Refine them as silver is refined,

And test them as gold is tested.

They will call on My name,

And I will answer them;

I will say, ‘They are My people,'

And they will say, ‘The Lord is my God.'"

13:7 There is an obvious radical break between Zech. 13:6 and 7. As 13:6 refers to false prophets (the
NET Bible thinks v. 7 is also against false prophets), 13:7 refers to the coming Messiah. Notice in your
translation that Zech. 13:1-6 is in prose, while Zech. 13:7-9 is poetry. This poetry is definitely related
to Zech. 11:4-14, which describes the godly shepherd.

▣ "Awake" This is a Qal IMPERATIVE (BDB 734, KB 802; NIDOTTE, vol. 3, pp. 357-359). The
VERB is used five times in Zechariah (cf. 2:13; 4:1 [twice]; 9:13; 13:7). It was imagery for calling on YHWH to act.

▣ "O sword" This is obviously a personification of death (cf. the VOCATIVE is also
used in Jer. 47:6-7 in a military sense). Notice that YHWH is the spokesman. He is the One who strikes the
Shepherd (cf. Ezekiel 21). The terms "awake" and "sword," in Zech. 13:7a, are both FEMININE,
while the word "strike" in Zech. 13:7d is Hiphil IMPERATIVE MASCULINE SINGULAR (BDB 645,
KB 697) and refers to YHWH striking the shepherd (i.e., vicarious substitutionary atonement, cf. Isa. 53:10; Mark 10:45;
Acts 2:23; 2 Cor. 5:21).

▣ "My Shepherd" This is an obvious reference to the Davidic king (cf. Zech. 12:10). "Shepherd"
originally referred to YHWH (cf. Psalm 23), but it is later used of the leaders of Israel (cf. Ezekiel 34). It
is used in the DSS and the NT to describe the Messiah (cf. John 10).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE DEITY OF
CHRIST FROM THE OT

▣ "And against the man, My Associate" The NIV translates this "and against the man who is close
to me." This is obviously a reference to a close associate (BDB 765). This is why identifying this shepherd
with the one in Zech. 11:17 is misleading. This term (BDB 765) is used only here and in the book of Leviticus
(cf. Lev. 5:21; 18:20; 19:15,17; 24:19; 25:14,15). It obviously means a close friend or covenant neighbor.

▣ "strike the shepherd" This VERB (BDB 645, KB 697) is a Hiphil
IMPERATIVE. The close friend will be attacked!

▣ "that the sheep may be scattered" The VERB (BDB 806 I, KB 918; NIDOTTE, vol. 3,
pp. 585-589) is a Qal IMPERFECT used as a JUSSIVE. This is used as a fulfillment
of the cursing section of Deut. 28:64. Jesus makes an allusion to this when He was arrested in the Garden of Gethsemane
(cf. Matt. 26:31; Mark 14:27).

I think it is surely possible that this context is referring to Jesus, thereby the judgment relates to the rebellion
of Israel in A.D. 66 with the destruction of Jerusalem by Rome in A.D. 70. If this is true, the 1/3
remnant refers to the believing Jewish church that fled to Pella. This possibility is somewhat new to me. I have been impressed
by Steve Gregg's lectures on YouTube of Zechariah 13 and 14 (see www.thenarrowpath.com). This viewpoint would be considered
a "partial preterist" position.

▣ "I will turn My hand against the little ones" The VERB (BDB 996 [top of, p. 999],
KB 1427, Hiphil PERFECT with waw) is used especially of YHWH's judgment
(cf. Isa. 1:25; Zech. 13:7; Ps. 81:15). The phrase "the little ones" is parallel to "the sheep," which are
scattered in the previous verse. This must be a time of testing initiated by YHWH Himself.

13:8 "That two parts in it will be cut off and perish;

But the third will be left in it" This seems to refer to some
type of punishment by YHWH where two-thirds of the people perish (i.e., Ezek. 5:1-4). This is either a reference to a military
invasion or to the spiritual rejection of the Messiah by two-thirds of God's people. Again, the time setting is ambiguous.

13:9 "And I will bring the third part through the fire,

Refine them as silver is refined,

And test them as gold is tested"

This refers to the purpose of refining (BDB 864, cf. Mal. 3:2) for strengthening
(cf. Isa. 48:10; Dan. 11:35). YHWH wants a purified people who reflect His character! This use of the
metallurgical term is quite common in the Bible to describe God testing His people (i.e., the faithful
remnant) for approval (cf. Prov. 17:3; Isa. 1:25; 48:10).

SPECIAL TOPIC: FIRE

SPECIAL TOPIC: GOD TESTS HIS PEOPLE

▣ "They will call on My name,

And I will answer them;

I will say, 'They are My people,'

And they will say, 'The Lord is my God'"

This is a series of covenant phrases (e.g., Hosea 2:19-23) to describe that in the midst of
YHWH's judgment on the shepherd and the sheep, His purpose is a stronger covenant relationship (cf. Zech. 8:8).

SPECIAL TOPIC: "THE NAME" OF YHWH (OT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: CALL ON THE NAME

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are
responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You,
the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this
section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- What is the historical setting of Zechariah 13?

- How is the unclean spirit related to the idols and prophets?

- Why is the false prophet in Zech. 13:3 pierced instead of being stoned?

- Was a hairy robe a sign of YHWH's prophets in the OT?

- List the major theological truths about the purpose of God in Zech. 13:7.

- How is Zechariah 13 related to Zechariah 11?

- Will only a remnant of Israel be saved? How does this apply or not apply to the church?
